clue.text: Low drawer?

parts.note: not a chest of drawers' bottom drawer but someone who draws pictures down on the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' reads as furniture; here it is a person who draws, working low down on the paving.
explanation.definitionFit: A street chalk artist makes pictures on the paving slabs at foot level, so is literally a low-down draughtsman.

clue.text: Regularly encountered faults in French article that's no good

indicators.note: only every other letter of the words is met along the way, starting with the first

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of faults in
le is the French masculine 'the'

explanation.surface: A grammar teacher dismisses an article written in French that keeps turning up mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters run over two words: F, U, T from faults and I from in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile is pointless and useless, achieving nothing worthwhile.

clue.text: Excavation made by feline on a search

parts.note: a cat is a feline
to comb is to search thoroughly; used here as a noun

explanation.surface: A cat digs a hole while hunting around for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground burial chambers dug out of rock, so one is a kind of excavation.

clue.text: Understanding him once person translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grasps what a figure from the past once said after rendering it into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Comprehension is the faculty of grasping meaning, a synonym of understanding.

clue.text: Quite partial to caramels or toffees

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being fairly fond of sweets like caramels and toffees.
explanation.definitionFit: Sort of is an informal hedge meaning to some extent, as quite can in British usage.

clue.text: Access two overlapping outdoor leisure areas

indicators.note: the two place names share a letter where one ends and the next begins, so one copy of it is dropped

parts.note: a rec (recreation ground) and a course (golf course) are both outdoor leisure areas

explanation.surface: Directions to two adjoining parks or sports grounds that share a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: REC and COURSE share the C, so they overlap into one word. A rec is the British name for a public recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is a means of turning to someone for help, i.e. access to a source of assistance.

clue.text: Flatterer to join you in the future, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means we hear it spoken, so the phrase is matched by sound

parts.words: to join you in the future
parts.note: to join you later is to add you later

explanation.surface: A sycophant promises to tag along with you at some later point.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulator heaps excessive praise on someone, the same as a flatterer or toady.

clue.text: Convincing firm fellow

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a gent is a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A sturdy chap who makes a persuasive case.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is clear and logical, therefore persuasive.

clue.text: Panicky figure admits wrongdoings with con

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the number holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
errors are wrongdoings or mistakes
a trick is a con, a swindle

explanation.surface: A nervous person confesses to misdeeds that included a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone terror-stricken is gripped by fear, a stronger version of being panicky.

clue.text: Cheerful one, new, announced welcome drinks

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the greeting is matched by its sound

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome
spirits are strong alcoholic drinks

explanation.surface: A happy host, newly arrived, declares that drinks will be served on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting HI is heard as HIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in high spirits is an idiom for being lively and happy.

clue.text: Plant in the morning removed from across the pond

indicators.note: removed from says the time abbreviation is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: from a British view, America lies across the pond, the Atlantic
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A plant is shipped off one morning from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus name for heath and heather plants.

clue.text: This compiler in noon trip served wine

indicators.note: in places the setter's pronoun within the rearranged letters
served as in a tennis serve or a dish served up, the letters are put out in a new order

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, giving I

explanation.surface: The setter is offered wine on a midday outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot Noir is a red grape variety and the red wine made from it, notably Burgundy.

clue.text: Having uncovered keys, behold den opening

indicators.note: each word loses its covering, its first and last letters

parts.note: keys without its outer letters
behold without its outer letters
den without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone with exposed keys spots a gap in a den.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyehole is a small hole to look through, so a kind of opening.

clue.text: Draw conclusions about back giving you hell

parts.note: to infer is to draw conclusions

indicators.note: back means the little word for about is read in reverse

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone works out that their bad back is torture.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is Dante's name for hell, and generally a hellish blaze.

clue.text: They fix last of bust sirens having received foreigner's cash

indicators.note: having received means the combined letters take the money inside them
only the final letter of bust is used

parts.note: hooters are sirens or horns
roubles are Russian money

explanation.surface: Fixers of broken alarms are paid in foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The roubles go in between the T of bust and HOOTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubleshooters are people hired to identify and solve problems, so they fix things.

clue.text: Covering area, suspect locusts dominate

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged insects wrap around the abbreviation
suspect as an adjective means dubious, signalling these letters are unreliable and reordered

explanation.surface: Swarms of locusts spread over a region and take over.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass rivals is to surpass them clearly, to beat them convincingly.

clue.text: Ability to speak about case in biased university shows persistence

indicators.note: about means going around, so the speaking skill surrounds the other letters

parts.note: oracy is fluency in speech, a counterpart of literacy

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: A debater's partial argument about a university case shows dogged stubbornness.
explanation.definitionFit: Obduracy is stubborn refusal to change one's mind, a dogged persistence.

clue.text: Group by a hill to the west turns round

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means reading from right to left

parts.note: a set is a group
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A band of people beside a hill on its western side keeps spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rotates spins on its axis, i.e. turns round.

clue.text: Time Out journalist praised

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A writer for the London listings magazine Time Out gave a glowing review.
explanation.definitionFit: To tout something is to promote or hype it up, which is a kind of praise.

clue.text: One wading quietly by lake bitten by snake

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: bitten by means the lake letter sits between the snake's jaws

parts.note: an adder is a snake
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone splashing about quietly by a lake gets bitten by a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler walks in shallow water at the seaside, i.e. someone wading.

clue.text: Carriage left with content of haul

parts.note: and means with, in addition to

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside its outer letters

explanation.surface: A carriage departs carrying a load of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding top.

clue.text: I'm going to gossip after Romeo's knocked out by husband showing bad temper

indicators.note: after places the contraction ahead of the gossip word

parts.note: I'll is short for I will, I'm going to

indicators.note: knocked out by means one letter is dislodged and another takes its place

parts.note: rumour is gossip
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone vows to spread tales once Romeo is floored by an angry husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill humour is a grumpy, irritable mood, the same as bad temper.

clue.text: Period in charge of old characters

parts.note: a run is a period or spell

explanation.surface: An era when elderly figures were in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic describes runes, the letters of the ancient Germanic alphabet.

clue.text: Sample duck taken from kitchen appliance

indicators.note: taken from means the zero letter is removed from the appliance

parts.note: a toaster is a kitchen appliance
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A cook samples some duck pulled out of a kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion offered to try, a sample.

clue.text: Barrier code, task to crack

indicators.note: to crack means to break apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A security fence whose code is a job someone must break.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive enclosure of posts, a barrier.
